analysis.investment_thesis: Exato is a recently listed micro-cap IT services firm trading at ~35x earnings and ~6.8x book value with only three years of audited results — failing nearly every quantitative filter I require. There is no margin of safety; the price embeds heroic growth assumptions that I refuse to underwrite.
key_strengths: Three consecutive years of positive net profit (5, 5, 10 Cr)
Promoter holding 54.73% provides skin in the game
key_risks: P/B ~6.8x and P/E 35 — no margin of safety vs. Graham number (~₹130 vs price ₹414)
Borrowings ballooned 6→17→28 Cr; D/E 0.56 exceeds my 0.5 ceiling
FY24 OCF was -14 Cr and FY25 FCF effectively zero — earnings not converting to cash
red_flags: Recently listed BSE micro-cap (symbol 544626) — insufficient 5-year earnings history
Rapid balance-sheet expansion funded by debt + equity issuance (financing CF 5→9→19 Cr)
IPO-era pricing — sellers/underwriters set the price, not the disciplined buyer
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a strict Graham lens, this security fails the most basic tests. Net worth is only ₹50 Cr against a market capitalization of ₹338 Cr — investors are paying nearly seven rupees for every rupee of book equity in a commoditized "IT enabled services" niche with no demonstrated moat. The Graham Number, computed at roughly ₹130 per share (sqrt(22.5 × 12.25 EPS × 61.3 BVPS)), is less than a third of the ₹414 quoted price. A P/E of 35 on a three-year-old earnings record is precisely the kind of speculative pricing Mr. Market offers to the impatient.

The operating story is not without merit — revenue grew 73→124 Cr and net profit doubled to 10 Cr in FY25 — but the cash flow tells a less flattering tale: FY24 operating cash flow was negative 14 Cr and cumulative three-year FCF is roughly negative 10 Cr, financed by ₹22 Cr of new borrowings and equity raises. This is a growth-funded enterprise, not a self-sustaining compounder. Until Exato delivers 5+ years of earnings, lowers leverage below 0.5x equity, and trades closer to book value, it remains squarely in the speculative bucket. Avoid.
